note: Per-subsystem judgment on why it carries host guards (isTauri / isHeadlessHost / usePlatform). Produced by `pnpm audit:host-parity:report` and classified by hand — the census is mechanical, the classification is not. `confidence: "low"` marks a row decided from naming and a spot check rather than a full read; those are where a reviewer should look first. Classifications: physically-impossible (the host genuinely lacks the surface), unmigrated (no physical reason — the work just was not done), ui-assumption (backend can reach parity; the UI keys off the host instead of a capability), seam-infrastructure (this IS the host-detection/transport layer; branching on host is its job).

components/automation.note: The consent overlay hides itself off-Tauri; once consent is remotable it should key off the capability instead.

components/boot.note: `usePlatform()` in boot-screen.tsx to pick the shell-appropriate boot presentation. A brain has no boot screen.

components/browser.note: Already degrades to RemoteBrowserPreview / iframe off-Tauri, and headless has the full browser.remote surface (28 ops). The guard should follow the capability.

components/desktop.note: Native window/menu chrome. Some children may be ui-assumption; split when paying down.

components/devices.note: Device controls and ownership candidates must be selected from runtime capabilities; the current guards still key presentation and grant affordances directly off the shell.

components/global-search.note: `usePlatform()` in the dialog for platform-appropriate chrome and shortcut hints (ADR-0129).

components/inbox.note: Adapter health/consent affordances gated on isTauri(); the connector runtime itself works headless.

components/pet.note: The in-page pet renders anywhere; only the overlay window is desktop-bound.

components/selection-toolbar.note: ADR-0093/0095 — needs a visible desktop and screen-recording permission.

components/settings.note: 145 guards / 93 files — the largest single cluster, and 21 sections are hard-marked `desktopOnly: true`. This is the primary target of the `desktopOnly → requires: [capability]` migration.

components/ui.note: `usePlatform()` in loading-states.tsx to fold host-specific boot phases (pairing, host, sync) into one timeline. Presentation only; components/ui is otherwise the untested shadcn tree.

components/workspace.note: One `isTauri()` in workspace-picker-list.tsx, and it is half right: the desktop opens a native folder dialog, while a paired phone or browser opens the HOST's tree through `fs_list_workspace_dir`. The capability half of that decision is already the gate (`gate("fs_list_workspace_dir").available`); the `isTauri()` beside it stands in for "can I show a native dialog", which is a UI question keyed off the host rather than off a capability. Only an unpaired browser genuinely has neither path.

hooks/devices.note: Device discovery and grant actions currently branch on Tauri even though Companion and remote-host transports expose capability-based equivalents.

hooks/global-search.note: `isTauri()` around the open-folder and check-updates palette actions, each falling back to a localized "desktop only" toast rather than failing silently, plus one `usePlatform()` for context assembly. Honest degradation, not a hidden gap.

hooks/sites.note: `use-site-action-gate.ts` reads `usePlatform()` to disable host-privileged Sites controls outside Tauri, and its own docblock names why the boundary is physical: builds run through `sandbox_exec`, previews spawn a PTY, provider tokens need the OS keyring, and the manifest lives on disk. Getting it wrong is worse than an error, because the keyring silently falls back to an in-memory store and a saved token would look accepted and vanish. The console renders on every host and disables with a reason rather than blanking, which is the shape this classification asks for.

hooks/terminal.note: Two guards. `use-ssh-host-key-change.tsx` gates TRUSTING a changed host key on `isTauri()`, because the known-hosts file it would write lives on the machine running the SSH client, and its comment says so. `use-terminal-autocomplete.ts` passes `detectPlatform()` as data for path-shape completion, which is a fact about the host being completed against rather than a branch.

lib/automation.note: AX/UIA against a real desktop. Consent is NOT in this category — see ADR-0059: it routes to a paired device via notifications.remote.

lib/browser.note: `installSnapshotInvalidation` gates on `isTauri()` because the snapshot-dirty event arrives on the Tauri event plane. The code already degrades honestly (the cache stays conservative and `fresh` bypasses it), so this is a missed optimisation on a cloud host rather than a broken feature — it clears when the browser events move onto the swappable seam.

lib/connectors.note: installConnectorRuntime gates on isTauri() and the brain bypasses it with skipHostGate. The transports themselves are migrated: all nine IM adapters subscribe through `connectorListen` (lib/connectors/events.ts), which is the only production file here importing @tauri-apps/api/event and is a declared SEAM_OWNER — so the four IM platforms that once could not receive on a cloud host now can. What remains is the bootstrap gate itself.

lib/docs-providers.note: This IS the host-support declaration for the cloud-document providers. `listAvailableDocsProviders` and `isDocsProviderHostSupported` filter a registry by each provider's own `hosts` list, which is the registry's job and the reason a mobile user sees WHY a provider is missing instead of an empty picker. The one `isTauri()` outside that, in `providers/google/http.ts`, picks the Tauri transport over `fetch` and is the same seam question.

lib/git.note: The git RPC arms carry NO host gate at all — they are host-neutral and work headless today. host-feature-manifest.ts still declares source-control.git as tauri-only (class E finding).

lib/keyring.note: Branches to the OS keyring on desktop and an AES-GCM IndexedDB blob elsewhere; headless uses cognia-secrets. Equivalent by construction, not a gap.

lib/native/codex-app-dispatch.ts.note: Drives the installed Codex DESKTOP app, not a service. `codex_app_dispatch.rs` resolves `~/.codex/app-server-control/app-server-control.sock` (`codex_home()`), and when that socket is absent `connect_or_launch` recovers by opening `codex://threads/new` through the OS URL-scheme handler — a container has neither the app nor a handler to register the scheme. Same footing as AX/UIA: the SUBJECT is missing, not the plumbing. Note the plumbing is in fact host-neutral (`run_cdp_control` shells a Node sidecar), so do not 'fix' this by making the sidecar host-agnostic — the socket still never appears. Reclassified 2026-08-16; the 2026-08-15 audit's "no physical reason found" was wrong.

lib/ocr.note: Only apple-vision and windows-media-ocr are physical; packages/ocr/src/registry.ts already subtracts exactly those two for headless. tesseract/ocrs/paddle run anywhere.

lib/platform.note: detect.ts + capabilities.ts + host-feature-manifest.ts — the tables themselves.

lib/plugin.note: The clearest case in the repo: rpc/plugins.rs has 52 headless-only arms and 12 desktop-only ones. The subsystem is split in half with neither side complete.

lib/signaling.note: desktop-controller.ts is a documented no-op off Tauri; the mobile mirror lives in transport-rtc.ts.

lib/support-report.note: Two guards: `clipboardAvailable()` probes the host so the copy button is never a silent no-op (legitimate), and the `crashReports` section declares `isAvailable: () => isTauri()`. A headless server produces native crash reports too, so that section is gated to the desktop by omission rather than by a physical boundary.

lib/tauri.note: 121 guards — the transport seam itself. `pickTransport()` choosing Tauri/Companion/WebStub per host is the mechanism parity rests on, not a gap in it.

lib/terminal.note: headless holds the `pty` capability and ws_terminal.rs already proxies real PTY frames over WS and WebRTC; pick-transport.ts still returns "unsupported" for anything that is not Tauri/Capacitor/remote-host.

lib/tray.note: OS tray needs a desktop session.

lib/tts.note: Synthesis is host-neutral; local audio playback may not be.

lib/vector.note: Native sqlite-vec throws a typed unsupported-platform error off-Tauri; cloud backends work anywhere.

packages/agent-config-types.note: The only guard token is documentation in the settings-sync contract explaining why machine-local wallpaper refs cannot cross hosts; no runtime branch exists in this package.
